is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies Anopheles gambiae complex mosquitoes.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports Vgsc L1014F and L1014S mutations.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper uses a collated dataset from Coleman et al. (26) and reports only aggregated allele frequencies (n=316 observations) rather than raw genotype counts or extractable genotype data for specific populations.

african_field_population.evidence: The study uses field-collected mosquito samples from 38 African countries.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a meta-analysis/statistical modeling paper that re-analyzes previously published data collated from other studies (Coleman et al. 2017).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study uses data from 1,183 locations across Africa.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study analyzes data collected over the period 2000–2015, but the modeling approach uses specific time-indexed data.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper explicitly states it is a meta-analysis using a dataset collated by Coleman et al. (2017) and that it re-analyzes previously published data.

supplement.evidence: The paper relies on a large collated dataset (Coleman et al. 26) and the specific per-site genotype counts are not provided in the main text or the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This paper is a meta-analysis that uses Bayesian geostatistical modeling to analyze the relationship between insecticide resistance phenotypes and Vgsc mutation frequencies across Africa using a collated dataset from previous studies.
exclusion_reasons: Not a primary empirical study (it is a meta-analysis/statistical modeling paper)
Does not report extractable raw genotype data (only aggregated allele frequencies)
